title: Resumable session handoff experiment log
content:
Summary:
This is an experimental log for a resumable-session / handoff protocol and client SDK ergonomics we ran across several prototype SDKs (JS, Swift, Kotlin) and the hosted runtime. The goal: let long-running streaming calls (multi-tool flows, progressive structured output) survive intermittent client disconnects, network changes, and mobile backgrounding with minimal developer-friction and predictable semantics for tool-calling (idempotency) and structured partial-output.

Goals / success criteria:
- Resume success rate >= 98% for reconnects within 60s on stable sessions.
- Mean time-to-resume (TTResume) < 350ms for resumed socket handshake after auth.
- No duplicate tool invocations visible to downstream systems (duplicate-tool-exec-rate < 0.1%).
- Structured-output integrity: partial JSON fragments rehydrate to valid top-level object after resume in > 99% of cases (accounting for minor field reordering).
- SDK ergonomics: integration requires <= 3 lines of developer code changes for typical streaming+tooling flows.

Hypotheses we tested:
1) A compact resume token containing (session-id, last-offset, kv-checksum) is sufficient for safe continuation and reduces server state retention by allowing stateless validation for short-lived resumes.
2) Sending a short preflight delta-check (client -> server) with the client-side last-observed action IDs prevents duplicate tool execution without heavy coordination.
3) Progressive structured-output should be made resumable by framing output as idempotent "atomic frames" (frame-id + type + payload) and allowing the client to request replays from a frame-id.
4) Mobile SDKs should expose an optional low-bandwidth resume mode that trades fidelity (no immediate tool tracing payloads) for faster resume handshake and lower data use when reconnecting over cellular.

Experimental setups (high-level):
- Runtime: hosted-api staging fleet (canary kernels) with prefix-caching + KV cache enabled for common models.
- Model profiles: small-chat-like (genesis-7B) and long-sequence summarizer (llama-13B variant).
- SDKs tested: JS (node/browser), Swift (iOS background/resume), Kotlin (Android foreground/background).
- Network conditions: good (10–50ms), intermittent 3G emulation (200–800ms), flaky (random disconnects, 5–30s).
- Tool-calls: synchronous external HTTP webhook, queued batch job (idempotency token tested), local DB mutation (simulated).

Protocol notes (design sketch implemented for tests):
- Frames: every incremental output from the model is wrapped as {frame_id, seq, kind: [text|json|tool-result|checkpoint], payload}. Frames are appended to a session journal on the runtime for N seconds (configurable TTL).
- Resume token: base64(session_id|last_frame_id|crc32(session_journal_tail)|expiry_ts|sig). Token validity window: 120s in experiments (tunable).
- Preflight delta: on reconnect, client sends resume_token + last_local_frame_id_seen list (comma-separated up to 10 entries). Server compares and returns either: ACCEPT + replay(start_frame) or REJECT (new session required).
- Tool call protections: each tool invocation includes a client-supplied idempotency_key (UUID) and the server ensures the effect is recorded atomically with the session journal frame. On resume, server will not re-execute tool-calls with observed idempotency keys.
- Checkpoint frames: SDKs can emit explicit checkpoints (user-visible commit points) that extend resume guarantees: runtime persists a compact snapshot (headers + latest kv-checksum) to longer TTL store.

SDK ergonomics we experimented with:
- Minimal API: session = client.openSession({model, streaming:true}); session.on('frame', cb); session.resume(resumeToken, opts); session.checkpoint();
- Higher-level: session.streamingCall(prompt, {onFrame, onToolCall}) returns object with resume() convenience wrapper.
- Mobile specifics: Swift/Kotlin adapters expose a backgroundResume(token, minimal=true) to reduce payloads until full app wake.
- Error handling: SDK surfaces 'resume_conflict' and 'resume_replayed' events; devs must be able to distinguish a normal resume (idempotent) vs forced session restart.
- Backpressure: client receives 'throughput_hint' frames from runtime indicating when to pause local buffering to avoid large replay windows.

Observability / telemetry captured:
- resume_attempts, resume_success, resume_latency_p50/95/99, resume_conflicts, duplicate_tool_rate, frames_replayed_count, session_journal_size_bytes, checkpoint_frequency, mobile_resume_mode_percentage.
- Trace correlation: every resume event emits trace with session_id and resume_token_masked for debugging.

Early results (summarized):
- Good networks: resume_success 99.6%, TTResume median 120ms.
- Intermittent 3G: resume_success 96.8% (failures mostly due to token expiry), TTResume median 420ms (above target).
- Flaky disconnects: resume_conflicts rose to 1.2% when clients raced to re-open the same session twice due to aggressive retry policies.
- Duplicate tool invocations: observed 0.3% in one test where client retried before receiving commit acknowledgement; fixed by making tool idempotency check canonical and moving commit acknowledgement into the journal append atomic step.
- Structured-output integrity: atomic-frame approach rehydrates reliably for text and simple JSON outputs, but large chunked JSON (multi-frame arrays) need explicit per-frame schema markers to avoid reassembly ambiguity.

Notable developer friction discovered:
- Many existing client implementations rely on naive reconnect heuristics (open new session if any error). Our suggested surface therefore must make restart explicit and easy (session.forceRestart()) so developers don't write fragile wrappers.
- Idempotency keys are easy to forget. SDKs must auto-generate idempotency keys for tool-call wrappers while allowing user override.
- Resume tokens are long and opaque; developer UX wants both a compact token for mobile and a human-readable short id for debugging.

Edge cases and unresolved questions:
- Cross-region resume: how to route a resume token if the client's session shifted to a different regional pool? We experimented with global token validation and lightweight handoff but saw 60–120ms added latency. Tradeoff: global validation vs. local sticky routing.
- Long tail sessions: sessions that run > 10 minutes accumulate large journals. We need eviction and checkpoint cadence rules to avoid storage blowup. Current heuristics: checkpoint every N tool-calls or every M seconds.
- Partial tool semantics: what counts as 'executed'? We currently mark tool-call committed when journal append and side-effect ack occurs. For external webhooks this can be slow; need standardized async-confirmation pattern and webhooks should return idempotency-ack quickly.

Actionable next steps (near term):
- (Jonas) Reduce default resume token TTL to 90s and add TTL tuning per-plan in console (RB). Monitor resume_success impact.
- (Liang) Implement automatic idempotency generation in JS & mobile SDKs and add opt-out flag for advanced users.
- (Aisha) Draft SDK docs + quickstart snippet showing 3-line integration for streaming+tools with resume tokens. Include migration notes for teams that do naive reconnects.
- (Samantha) Add resume telemetry dashboards to Console: resume success, TTResume p95, duplicate_tool_rate, frames_replayed histogram.
- Add integration tests in runtime that simulate region-handoff and measure extra latency; evaluate global token validation vs sticky routing.

Longer-term decisions to surface to PM/ENG:
- Whether to guarantee cross-region resume or document regional resumes as best-effort. Cross-region adds infra complexity but UX benefit for multi-region mobile roamers.
- Formal resume API shape (compact token vs. JSON token) for enterprise customers who want forward compatibility guarantees.
- Productizing checkpointing with a low-cost storage tier for long-running sessions as a paid feature for Dedicated/Private customers.

Appendix: quick dev examples (JS-like pseudocode)
- Open and resume:
  const s = client.openSession({model:'genesis-7B', streaming:true});
  s.on('frame', (f) => render(f));
  // when backgrounding
  const token = s.checkpoint(); // small opaque string
  // on restart
  client.resumeSession(token).then(s2 => s2.on('frame', cb));

- Tool call wrapper that auto idempotentizes:
  await s.callTool('create-order', {items}, {idempotencyKey: s.autoId()});

Notes to self / TODOs (working):
- Capture failure traces for the 3.2% resume failures under 3G to determine if we should extend token TTL or implement token refresh.
- Run A/B on default retry behavior in SDKs: exponential backoff vs immediate restart.
- Check legal implications for auditability when we suppress tool-call payloads in mobile low-bandwidth resume mode.

Status: Draft experiment log — share with runtime, SDK, and solutions-eng for feedback. Once we consolidate telemetry and fix the idempotency edge we've observed, propose as a beta feature behind a feature flag (hosted-api:resumable-sessions) for a subset of customers.
